Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

Money as a Service (MaaS) oversees a diverse portfolio of Stripe's core products and platforms, and our vision is to become the financial operating system for platforms and marketplaces globally. These offerings facilitate the global movement and management of funds for users.

The teams that fall under the MaaS umbrella are Connect, Money Management, and Crypto. Together, these teams work to ensure Stripe users have the robust financial infrastructure and tools they need to power their businesses on a global scale.

As a TPM, you will play a key role leading complex programs across multiple engineering, product and cross-functional (finance, legal, compliance, risk, and other) teams spanning Stripe. You will be responsible for the successful definition, cross-functional strategy, planning and execution of large-scale technical programs that help to solve complex problems and empower Stripe and our users.

· Independently define, scope, and drive functional and technical delivery of key team and org-wide programs/initiatives.

· Partner with Engineering Managers, Product Managers and other cross-functional partners to define, scope, and drive large programs to conclusion.

· Develop, implement, and iterate on program management techniques, frameworks, and KPIs to achieve goals with well-defined success criteria.

· Make substantial improvements to how the teams you work with communicate and operate to significantly increase productivity and efficiency.

· Define and produce high quality written proposals, communications and documentation.

· Leverage data and acquired knowledge to inform technical decisions and contribute to your organization's strategy.

· Create widely circulated plans, driving consistency, clarity and building alignment across teams.

· Help influence peers / leaders and build consensus while dealing with ambiguity.

· Mentor new TPMs and actively contribute to the TPM hiring process.

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

· 6+ years of software engineering, systems engineering and/or technical program management experience.

· Excellent analytical skills; you digest complex information and make recommendations.

· You have a track record of independently managing programs across all phases of software development from kick-off to launch, demonstrating critical thinking, challenging the norms and thought leadership.

· You have very strong written and verbal communication skills, building strong relationships with stakeholders, teams and senior leaders around the organization.

· You can drive internal and external process improvements across multiple teams and functions and bring a wealth of experience, opinions, proposals and best practices.

· Experience operating autonomously and leading large-scale efforts across multiple teams and functions, with stakeholders in different disciplines across time zones.

· Ability to understand how functionality comes together (across products and platforms) to deliver value for users, and identify/mitigate delivery risks proactively; can propose and drive a technical solution.

· Users-first and customer-focused mindset.

·

· Experience in a global FinTech or banking organization.

Who we are
About Bridge
We're creating an entirely new payments platform, built with stablecoins, to simplify global money movement. Bridge enables faster, cheaper payments and borderless access to dollars via stablecoins. Through our APIs, businesses can send and receive funds across borders faster and cheaper vs. SWIFT and other fiat-only rails.

Our virtual accounts enable international consumers and businesses to easily access, store, and spend US dollars. Our payouts infrastructure enables platforms to disburse USD to anyone globally. We believe many trillions of dollars will move and settle through stablecoin payment rails. Bridge is pulling this future forward.
We have a small team of people who have previously built financial infrastructure at some of the world's leading companies (Coinbase, Stripe, Square, Brex, Upstart, DoorDash, Airbnb), and each and every one of them chose Bridge because they fundamentally believe that stablecoins will be a critical piece of financial infrastructure that allows for the improvement of global money movement.

Join our Technical Program Management team to build the systems that make global, programmable money trustworthy at scale. At Bridge, we’re not just improving global payments—we’re reinventing how money moves across borders using stablecoins and modern financial infrastructure.
This role is about driving execution across complex technical initiatives—bringing structure to ambiguous problems, aligning stakeholders, and helping the team move quickly while maintaining reliability, performance, and operational excellence.

As a TPM, you'll play a key role leading complex programs across multiple engineering, product, and cross-functional (finance, legal, compliance, risk, and other) teams spanning Bridge.

You'll be an active contributor to the overall strategy of the program, drive technical decision-making, and drive the execution of the program through all phases from planning to delivery. You'll have the opportunity to implement mechanisms that make your programs effective and scale them to Bridge-level processes.

Drive functional and technical delivery of key team and org-wide programs and initiatives.
Collaborate with engineering teams to design, scope, and shepherd features.
Create functional specs, project and release plans, and roadmaps.
Own and execute one or more software engineering programs simultaneously.
Drive product decisions that align with program and company objectives
Influence senior stakeholders and build consensus across engineering, product, and cross-functional teams
Define and scale program processes and frameworks that can be adopted across the org
Mentor TPMs and contribute to building the TPM discipline at Bridge

6+ years of experience in technical program or product management, with a consistent track record of shipping products with broad and global customer impact
You have a track record of providing solid program management during all phases of software development from kick-off to ship, demonstrating critical thinking and thought leadership throughout.
You're not satisfied with just delivering programs on time—you're discerning about product and infrastructure architecture and can lead technical discussions. You don’t let problems remain ambiguous and directly drive clarity on decision tradeoffs and solutions.
You operate independently and lead efforts across multiple teams and functions, with stakeholders in different disciplines across time zones.
You have strong written and verbal communication skills to build relationships and collaborate with diverse cross-functional teams

Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

Link is one of the fastest-growing consumer networks in the world, with 300M+ registered consumers. Our core mission is to make commerce seamless, helping merchants drive material gains in conversion and cost savings, while giving consumers a flexible and frictionless digital wallet they love. We're expanding beyond payments into identity and consumer finance, building the premier consumer network for next-generation commerce.
In this role, you'd be joining a team that operates at the intersection of consumer experience, payments infrastructure, and financial products.

Link spans multiple interconnected workstreams, including payment methods, money movement, fraud and authorization, consumer accounts and identity, and consumer preference, and a TPM here plays a critical role in keeping those threads aligned and moving forward at velocity.

Additionally, you’ll work to build integrations between Link and many other parts of Stripe.

Effective Technical Program Managers at Stripe always bias towards driving the right solutions for internal and external users, and delivering impact above all else. You'll do this even when it's not the easiest path, and requires difficult trade-off decisions.

In this role, you'll help Link scale its consumer network and expand into new product surfaces by driving complex, cross-functional programs that span engineering, product, fraud, identity, and business teams.

You'll look ahead and around corners to enable our teams to operate at their best, and identify opportunities to eliminate the unnecessary in delivering results.

Independently define programs across Link's payment, identity, and consumer finance initiatives, including scoping, setting objectives, defining success criteria, and influencing resource allocation to deliver outcomes
Apply consistent prioritization and decision-making frameworks across your programs, driving high-velocity yet durable decisions that move the team forward without creating downstream debt
Identify obstacles and risks across Link's cross-functional workstreams, proactively communicate them to stakeholders, and develop plans to address and prevent their recurrence
Represent the voice of Link's consumers and merchants to all stakeholders, translating user needs into clear program objectives and ensuring engineering and product decisions remain grounded in solving real problems
Drive clarity across all stakeholders on goals, problems, and intended outcomes, serving as the connective tissue across Link sub-teams and their upstream and downstream dependencies. Operate similarly across Stripe, representing the Link org to collaborators in peer organizations.
Develop a strong point of view on Link's product development strategy and use it to define programs with measurable outcomes, adapting them as the product and user needs evolve
Understand the technical challenges across Link's systems, payment flows, identity infrastructure, fraud and risk models, money movement, and partner closely with engineering leads to define the most effective path to delivery

Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase , we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits.

If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” learn more about working at Coinbase .
The Enterprise Applications & Architecture (EAA) Business Unit Delivery team builds and operates the internal platforms that help Coinbase scale.

Within EAA, the Compliance CX Agent Experience team owns Agent Cockpit, the primary internal platform used by Coinbase's compliance agents and investigators to review cases, communicate with customers, access account and transaction data, and resolve compliance-related support queries.

As a Staff Technical Program Manager, you'll own program delivery for this complex, high-impact platform, driving cross-functional execution to ensure agents and investigators have reliable, performant tools every day.

Own the program management framework for Agent Cockpit, including roadmap tracking, intake and prioritization, sprint planning, dependency management, and cross-team delivery execution.
Drive technical dependency coordination and platform migrations, translating upstream system changes (API deprecations, service integrations, data model changes) into internal delivery plans and engineering asks.
Lead launch readiness and operational risk management, owning security review coordination, production approvals, testing governance, and escalation when critical-path items stall.
Partner with Engineering on reliability, observability, and performance programs, including system health metrics, load testing, capacity planning, and backend monitoring to ensure platform stability at scale.
Manage cross-functional alignment across Engineering, Product, Security, Payments, Compliance Operations, and CX leadership, owning the rolling intake process for partner team requests and communicating prioritization decisions.
Support agent enablement by maintaining access patterns, JIT flows, role-based access guidance, and operational runbooks for agents, team leads, L&D, and partner engineering teams.

8+ years of technical program management experience, including leading complex, multi-stakeholder programs in platform or internal-tools environments.
Proven experience coordinating engineering dependency management and API/interface migrations across teams when upstream platforms change, with the ability to translate technical complexity into clear delivery plans.
Demonstrated ability to drive security reviews, launch-readiness processes, and operational risk workflows in production environments, including capacity planning, observability, and performance measurement.
Experience working in regulated or compliance-heavy environments with internal users such as investigators, agents, or operations teams, operating as the sole program leader across highly technical stakeholders.
Experience applying Agile, Lean, or similar delivery frameworks to real-world execution, with experience managing technical backlogs and writing technical PRDs.
Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality.

Our mission at Duolingo is to develop the best education in the world and make it universally available. It’s a big mission, and that’s where you come in!
At Duolingo, you’ll join a team that cares about finding innovative solutions to complex technical problems , running countless experiments (300+ at a time!) with our massive user base to make data-driven decisions, and educating our users and employees alike. You’ll have limitless learning opportunities, mentorship and collaboration with world-class minds, and a variety of projects with large scopes — while doing work that’s both fun and meaningful.
Join our life-changing mission to develop education for our half a billion (and growing!) learners around the world.

This is a high-impact, high-visibility Staff TPM role at the center of one of Duolingo's most strategic engineering initiatives: dramatically reducing the effort required to get results and doubling developer productivity across the organization.

You'll lead this initiative in close partnership with the Developer Amplification (DevAmp) Area, a team dedicated to accelerating how engineers work through better tooling, streamlined processes, and modern engineering practices.

AI is one important lever — but the goal is the outcome: step-change improvements in how fast and effectively Duolingo engineers can build. This role is for a builder and a change agent: someone who can define what "doubling productivity" means in practice, align leadership and engineering teams around it, and drive the transformation to completion.

If you thrive in ambiguity, have a bias for outcomes, and can bring people along through significant organizational change, this role is for you.
🧠 You will...
Define and drive the roadmap for doubling developer productivity across Duolingo — aligning engineering, product, and data science around a shared vision, sequencing the work, and holding teams accountable to measurable outcomes.
Lead organizational change management as engineering teams adopt new ways of working — building alignment, communicating progress to executives and ICs alike, and helping teams internalize new processes and tooling.
Partner closely with Developer Amplification (DevAmp) Area leads to accelerate developer productivity through AI-powered tooling, ensuring programs have clear goals, measurable impact, and sustained momentum across engineering squads.
Lead the delivery of strategic, high-impact cross-functional initiatives from conceptualization to launch, operating with significant autonomy across multiple workstreams.
Partner with engineering, product, data science, QA, and executive leadership to ensure communication and alignment; serve as the connective tissue between Duolingo strategy and day-to-day execution.
Leverage deep technical expertise to develop detailed plans with key milestones and goals, identify and mitigate risks, resolve dependencies, remove blockers, and ensure timely and smooth launches.
Establish and evangelize engineering practices that drive step-change improvements in developer productivity — coaching engineering leads and TPMs on new ways of working and how to measure their impact.
Drive decisions when difficult tradeoffs must be made, including those with cross-organizational or company-level impact; model how to navigate hard problems with analytical rigor and a calm, decisive presence.
Identify systemic issues impacting delivery efficiency company-wide and take swift, collaborative action to resolve them.
Guide and develop other TPMs and engineering leads, scaling best practices across teams and continuously improving how the organization operates.
✅ You have...
Proven experience as a TPM, Engineering Lead, or Engineering Manager.
B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science or equivalent degree or experience.
Demonstrated experience leading large-scale technical transformation programs with measurable organizational impact — you've shifted how engineering organizations think and work, not just shipped projects.
Strong executive presence and influence in a matrix environment — able to build conviction among skeptics, align competing priorities across senior leadership, and drive decisions without direct authority.
Deep technical credibility — enough to challenge architectural assumptions, spot delivery risks early, and earn the trust of strong engineers.
Proven ability to build and implement detailed plans that account for ambiguity, dependencies, and technical complexity — and to re-plan quickly when things change, without losing team confidence or momentum.
A track record of standing up new programs or practices from scratch in ambiguous, high-visibility environments.
Ability to relocate to Seattle, WA.
⭐ Exceptional candidates will have...
Strong knowledge of software engineering, systems engineering, or similar hands-on technical experience, in addition to program management experience.
Strong conceptual fluency in LLM-based products, AI infrastructure, and developer AI tooling - enough to ask the right questions, challenge technical assumptions, and identify delivery risks.
Experience running programs that include machine learning, large datasets, or AI/ML infrastructure.
Experience working with AWS at scale.

At Databricks, our core principles are at the heart of everything we do; creating a culture of proactiveness and a customer-centric mindset guides us to create a unified platform that makes data science and analytics accessible to everyone. As a Senior TPM, you lead the charge in changing how people work with data.

You will drive high-stakes, multi-workstream programs that have a material impact on customer success and scalability. Your technical expertise and strategic influence will be critical for guiding complex engagements to success and fostering a culture of continuous improvement.

You'll work with a collaborative, customer-focused team that values innovation and creativity, using your skills to create customized solutions to help our customers achieve their goals.
The Impact You Will Have
Architecting Standards : You will install operating rigor (cadence, metrics, reviews) that doesn't just serve one project, but becomes a "gold standard" adopted by other TPMs across the region.
Cross-Functional Synergy : You will lead high-visibility initiatives that require deep collaboration across Product, Engineering, and Marketing, resolving complex misalignments with M6-level Directors that threaten project velocity.
Strategic Risk Leadership : You will manage the change management process for large-scale digital transformations, ensuring that customer organizations are culturally and technically ready to adopt the Lakehouse architecture.
Knowledge Multiplication : You will contribute significantly to the Databricks community by documenting best practices and leading internal training sessions to level up the entire Professional Services organization.
What We Look For
Experience : 8–12+ years leading large-scale technical programs.
Technical Fluency : Advanced technical fluency; 2 Databricks Associate Certifications or 1 Professional-level Certification required within 6 months of hire.
AI Strategy : Proven track record of leveraging AI-enabled tools to optimize large-scale program delivery and cross-functional synergy.
Senior Leadership : Proven ability to engage, influence, and build trust with senior executive stakeholders (CxOs).
Scope : Experience successfully managing projects with teams of up to 5 people and contract values in excess of $0.5M.

As a Sr. Field Technical Program Manager (TPM) role in our Forward Deployed Engineering team, you will play a pivotal role in delivering complex technical projects that drive customer success and our business growth. Forward Deployed Engineering is part of the Field Engineering (FE) organization, the technical arm of Databricks’ customer-facing teams.
The TPM position understands our customers’ business goals and can steer technical projects from beginning to end with exceptional outcomes.

You will start on projects after a statement of work is agreed (i.e. post-sales) and will leverage your technical expertise and project management skills to navigate customer challenges and deliver with excellence at every stage.This role serves as the essential link between the Field Engineering teams and internal groups, including Sales, Product, and Engineering.

Customer Outcomes: Own delivering customer outcomes for approximately five concurrent customer projects, ensuring high customer satisfaction
Project Planning: Develop detailed technical project plans from finalized proposals or statements of work setting specific milestones, objectives, and key results.
Project Execution & Risk Management: Drive measurable weekly progress with detailed tracking and by mitigating risks to project objectives, ensuring projects stay on track.
Stakeholder Management: Facilitate effective meetings across technical and non-technical stakeholders, from engineering standups to executive steering committees.
Leadership: Adapt to changing project requirements and priorities, proactively steering projects around challenges and collaborating across Professional Services, Engineering, and Sales teams.
Technical Knowledge: Leverage and expand your understanding of data platform technologies and processes, such as data lakes, data governance, data quality, ETLs, and migration best practices, to drive customer outcomes faster.
Process Improvement: Define and implement new processes and operational cadences to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the Professional Services team.

Experience: 5+ years of experience in Technical Program Management, preferably in a B2B SaaS, cloud, or data engineering/analytics company.
Technical Background: A Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Must be comfortable diving deep into technical topics with Solution Architects and Engineers.
Program Management Skills: Proven ability to manage complex, cross-functional technical programs and deliver results in a fast-paced environment. Strong understanding of Agile and other program management methodologies.
Communication: Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex technical concepts to diverse audiences (from engineers to executives) and build consensus.
Domain Knowledge: Foundational knowledge of the data and AI landscape (e.g., data warehousing, data lakes, ETL, streaming, data science, machine learning).

Certifications: PMP, CSM, or related program management certification.
Databricks/Spark: Hands-on experience with the Data Intelligence Platforms or Data frameworks like Apache Spark™.
Cloud Platforms: Experience with public cloud provider solutions (AWS, Azure, or GCP).
Customer-Facing Experience: Prior experience in a customer-facing implementation role (e.g., Technical Project Manager, Solutions Architect, Technical Account Manager, Professional Services, Product Manager).
GenAI/ML Experience: Experience delivering programs related to AI, Machine Learning, or Generative AI.

As a Sr. Field Technical Program Manager at Databricks, you will be a key driver in our Forward Deployed Engineering team's mission to accelerate and de-risk customer outcomes. Your role is central to achieving project goals and maintaining exceptional customer satisfaction, particularly within our Canadian customer base.

While you are not expected to have hands-on coding experience, your technical acumen and strategic influence will be critical for guiding complex engagements to success. You will work closely with cross-functional teams to deliver excellence at every stage.
The Impact You Will Have
Be responsible for the successful delivery of our most complex customer engagements by providing technical leadership and guidance to the implementation team.
Guide technical teams through key architectural decisions, helping them navigate trade-offs between established and innovative approaches.
Proactively identify and mitigate technical risks and dependencies that could impact project timelines and goals.
Individually deliver on commitments by producing high-quality deliverables, status reports, program plans, and customer responses that require minimal rework.
Effectively manage all aspects of a program, including scope, schedule, budget, risk, and resources, with a focus on technical complexity.
Act as the primary point of escalation for customers regarding technical delivery issues and, as needed, escalate to other parts of Databricks for rapid resolution.
Build trust and credibility with technical teams and stakeholders by clearly articulating Databricks’ vision and solutions and facilitating productive, goal-oriented meetings.

Technical Acumen & Decision Making: A proven ability to stay current on technology trends and make sound technical decisions without being a hands-on coder.
Program & Project Management: Experience managing large, complex engagements and mitigating unexpected technical challenges. Familiarity with managing the trade-offs between scope, budget, and timeline.
Communication & Leadership: Excellent communication, negotiation, and conflict resolution skills. A track record of influencing technical teams and effectively tailoring messages for different audiences, from engineers to executives.
Experience with BI, data management, and big data technologies is preferred.
Proven ability to multitask and manage multiple engagements while delivering a high level of customer satisfaction.

We are looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to own new product introduction inside Revenue Operations and to build NPI into a discipline. As this is the first TPM on the team, and you will define the process from the ground up. NPI is how ClickHouse brings new products to market.

Stand up NPI as a repeatable discipline. Build the launch process, the requirements framework, and the operating cadence from a near-blank slate, and set the standard the rest of the org runs against.

About Phaidra
Phaidra is building the future of industrial automation.
The world today is filled with static, monolithic infrastructure. Factories, power plants, buildings, etc. operate the same they've operated for decades — because the controls programming is hard-coded. Thousands of lines of rules and heuristics that define how the machines interact with each other. The result of all this hard-coding is that facilities are frozen in time, unable to adapt to their environment while their performance slowly degrades.
Phaidra creates AI-powered control systems for the industrial sector, enabling industrial facilities to automatically learn and improve over time. Specifically:
We use reinforcement learning algorithms to provide this intelligence, converting raw sensor data into high-value actions and decisions.
We focus on industrial applications, which tend to be well-sensorized with measurable KPIs — perfect for reinforcement learning.
We enable domain experts (our users) to configure the AI control systems (i.e. agents) without writing code. They define what they want their AI agents to do, and we do it for them.
Our team has a track record of applying AI to some of the toughest problems. From achieving superhuman performance with DeepMind's AlphaGo , to reducing the energy required to cool Google's Data Centers by 40%, we deeply understand AI and how to apply it in production for massive impact.
Phaidra’s ability to achieve its mission is determined by our ability to work together — as defined by our core values: Transparency , Collaboration , Operational Excellence , Ownership , and Empathy. We seek individuals who embody these values, as they are instrumental in ensuring our team consistently delivers excellence and fosters an engaging and supportive culture
Phaidra is based in the USA, but we are 100% remote with no physical office. We hire employees internationally with the help of our partner, OysterHR . Our team is currently located throughout the USA, Canada, UK, Sweden, Spain, Portugal, the Netherlands, Singapore, Australia, and India.

How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles.

We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Join the team as our next Senior Technical Program Manager, Service Delivery Systems on the Global Customer Services (GCS) Strategy & Operations team.

You'll design and build systems, including AI workflows that operate within the Customer Experience Operations (CXO) governance model and you'll be accountable to GCS business outcomes: resolution rates, revenue-per-headcount, product adoption and more.

Architect and build the systems that encode how GCS operates — account health observability, intelligent routing, knowledge retrieval, and workflow automation across our TAM, PS, and EM motions; including cost optimization.

Instrument everything you build — retrieval accuracy, action success rates, deflection, and failure patterns — and tie technical performance to GCS outcomes like time to value, resolution rate, cost-per-ticket, and time-to-resolution.
Translate complex system behavior into plain language for director and executive audiences while producing clear technical documentation for the teams who depend on your systems.

Gusto is becoming an AI-native company, and that only works if our security posture keeps pace. As the Vulnerability Management Technical Lead, you'll own the definition and delivery of Gusto's vulnerability management and security operations programs across Security, AIT, R&D, Infrastructure, GRC, and Risk.

You'll drive the centralized vulnerability scorecard, expand detection and monitoring coverage, harden the SDLC, and stand up the security metrics leadership runs the business on.

You'll drive the timelines, manage the dependencies, head off the risk, and use AI plugins to do the work itself, so security becomes something that helps Gusto move faster instead of slowing it down.

The TPM organization is part of our AIT, Risk, and Security team. We deliver the cross-functional work that lets Gusto securely accelerate its AI and platform modernization.

The vulnerability management and security operations programs sit right at the intersection of security engineering, infrastructure, and GRC, and they're foundational to how Gusto scales its AI ambitions safely. This is one of the most strategic programs on the team, and you'll lead it across a complex, fast-moving group of stakeholders.

Set the strategy and the roadmap
Work with leaders across Security, AIT, R&D, Infrastructure, GRC, and Risk to shape where vulnerability management and security operations go as Gusto becomes an AI-native company. Define what good vulnerability management and security operations look like for an AI-first business, and set the multi-quarter vision that gets us there.

Run intake and prioritization with senior stakeholders, and make the call on what gets built first. Decide where security should clear the way for AI speed and where it needs to hold the line, and bring leaders along on the why.

Put AI plugins to work to pull together stakeholder input, map dependencies, and keep the roadmap grounded in what's really happening.
Run the programs and the change
Lead delivery of the centralized vulnerability management program: coverage across code, cloud, data, and edge; CSPM/DSPM, container scanning, dependency and secrets detection, and owner-based remediation routing to closure.
Lead security operations delivery: expand high-risk detection and alerting across systems and vendors, impersonation and privileged-access logging, SIEM integration, insider-risk telemetry, and logging of agentic activity.
Stand up the daily security-health and vulnerability-management metrics dashboards leadership uses to run the business, and drive monthly vulnerability reporting.
Build security workflows that run on AI plugins by default, so coverage checks and evidence collection happen automatically instead of by hand.
Build the plans, manage scope and risk, track milestones, and deliver against every audit and regulatory commitment.
Roll out new controls, like risk-scored PR review, JIT privileged access, and secrets management, and help teams adopt them with training, comms, and runbooks that plugins keep up to date for you.
Keep a busy, fast-moving group of stakeholders aligned with clear, steady updates on where things stand.
Manage stakeholders and vendors
Hold vendors and partners to their commitments and push them toward AI-forward ways of working.
Stay on top of how every workstream is tracking, raise flags early, and get teams unstuck when they stall.
Watch the program budget, tooling spend, and implementation costs.

A history of taking programs from ambiguous to shipped in regulated environments.
5 to 8+ years leading cross-functional TPM or delivery work, with real time spent on security, infrastructure, or platform engineering.
A solid handle on vulnerability management and security operations, from scanning coverage and remediation SLAs to detection engineering, SIEM/monitoring, and identity and privileged access, and a sense for how they help Gusto move faster on AI.
A way of working where AI plugins drive your everyday delivery, and you help the people around you work the same way.
The ability to speak the language of security engineering, infrastructure, GRC, and R&D, and keep everyone rowing together.

Familiarity with the modern security stack, including vulnerability and asset scanners (e.g., Wiz, Axonius), code security (dependency and secret scanning), SIEM/detection (e.g., Panther), and identity/JIT access (e.g., Opal).
Hands-on experience using AI clients and plugins (MCPs) to generate program artifacts and take the busywork off your plate.
A working knowledge of control frameworks like SOC 1/2 and ISO 27001, plus secure SDLC practices.
A PM certification (PMP, CAPM, Scrum, or Prosci) and time spent in high-growth fintech or another regulated, fast-paced industry.

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. As a Technical Program Manager within the Enterprise Data Governance team, you will drive strategic execution across our core data governance processes.

Your primary focus is to protect member privacy safeguarding personal information through secure handling, processing, and storage to ensure trust, enforce compliance, and mitigate data exposure risks.

You will bridge the gap between corporate data governance policy and operational engineering, leading high-visibility technical programs that secure, classify, and institutionalize data controls across key data platforms.
As a leader, you will partner with engineering, the CIO organization, Legal, Privacy Compliance, and broader stakeholders to shield enterprise data frameworks while accelerating feature delivery.

Own the end-to-end strategy, roadmap, and execution of complex, multi-platform data privacy and data protection initiatives, driving the Privacy Rights Management (PRM) program as a primary priority.
Partner with engineering and platform teams to translate abstract data governance and privacy policies into actionable technical execution. Own the requirements lifecycle by authoring comprehensive PRDs, defining functional data controls, and ensuring engineering teams have the clear technical specifications needed for deployment.
Operationalize privacy lifecycles from intake through fulfillment, including the development of automated tools, management of Data Subject Access Requests (DSARs), and establishing governance SOPs for regulatory change management, data onboarding/offboarding, operational metrics, and control validation.
Operationalize the First Line of Defense (1LOD) ownership model to ensure compliance with evolving U.S. state, international, and SMB privacy obligations, ensuring governance frameworks are scalable and robust.
Manage the governance standards for both affiliate and non-affiliate data sharing, ensuring full alignment with privacy standards and internal policies. Act as a strategic contributor to core governance pillars, shaping frameworks for Metadata, Data Lineage, Data Retention, and Data Quality.
Own key metrics and controls to track and provide actionable insights to drive continuous improvement. Propose scalable, incremental counter-proposals to keep the business agile while overseeing asset-level metadata, Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) blueprints, and operational egress/ingress integration for data platforms and enterprise SaaS applications.
Collaborate with federated teams to institutionalize ownership matrices, translate complex regulatory mandates into actionable product requirements. Maintain focus on strategic priorities and outcome-driven execution when navigating ambiguous problems, ensuring clear communication of program status, risks, and mitigation plans to executive leadership.

Bachelor’s degree or higher with practical experience in a technical field.

Toast creates technology to help restaurants and local businesses succeed in a digital world, helping business owners operate, increase sales, engage customers, and keep employees happy.
Toast IQ is our agentic platform for restaurant operators: a growing set of specialized AI agents that take real work off an operator's plate — driving demand, managing labor, and optimizing the back office. We're launching new agents continuously across multiple lines of business, and the complexity of doing that well, with coherent packaging, consistent quality, and a single platform story, is growing faster than the surface area of the product itself.
This role owns the program that makes it work. You'll design and run the monthly release engine end to end, set and hold the bar on platform readiness, and coordinate go-to-market so naming, packaging, and messaging land as a coherent platform story rather than a dozen separate launches that confuse operators and the field. The goal is to build repeatable operating mechanisms that let Toast move quickly and confidently and that scale as Toast IQ scales.
You'll work across product, engineering, marketing, support, and finance. You won't have direct authority over most of the people you depend on, which means you'll earn influence, make decisions that stick, and serve as an escalation point when things go sideways.

Design, own, and continuously improve the monthly agent release program — one cadence, one launch process — across all lines of business. Build this as a durable operating mechanism, not a series of one-off coordination efforts.
Set and hold the platform-readiness bar. Engage credibly with engineering teams on architecture, dependencies, and technical risk. Own the dependency and risk map. Be willing to call a postponement when a product isn't ready — and make that call stick.
Drive go-to-market coherence across LOBs so naming, packaging, and messaging land as one platform story. Work with PMM and GTM to make sure the field can sell and operators understand what they're getting.
Instrument launch health and build reporting that matters: what shipped, what slipped, adoption signals, and the blockers that need to be resolved upstream. Feed this signal back to R&D leadership in a form they can act on.
Operate with high judgment in ambiguous situations. When the governance model doesn't cover a case, make a defensible call and move. Surface the right decisions to leadership with the context they need — don't just escalate problems.
Establish the operating rhythms, governance structures, and cross-functional alignment mechanisms that keep multiple engineering teams moving toward a shared cadence.

12+ years of technical program management working directly with software engineering teams.
Track record of owning cross-functional programs end to end — not just coordinating them — from design through launch, across teams with competing priorities.
Technical fluency sufficient to engage meaningfully with engineers on architecture, dependencies, and risk: you can identify when a technical assumption is wrong before it becomes a launch problem.
Demonstrated ability to build repeatable operating models. You've built the system, not just run projects inside someone else's system.
Experience managing cross-org dependencies and aligning teams you don't control.
Strong written communication; you can translate complex program status and risk into a clear narrative for senior leadership.

As a Senior Staff Technical Program Manager for Body, Closures & Chassis, you will serve as the Program Lead for our Body, Closures & Chassis Systems. You will provide the overarching technical direction and leadership required to guide the vehicle program from concept through production across Body, Closures, and Chassis domains.

In this position, you will bridge the gap between high-level program milestones and deep technical execution. You are responsible for balancing performance attributes, cost, quality, and manufacturability while coordinating engineering execution across our internal team and external partners.

Serve as the program and technical lead for the vehicle program across Body (BIW, structures), Closures (doors, mechanisms, glazing), and Chassis (suspension, subframes, tires, wheels, by-wire systems), collaborating with internal engineers and external supplier design teams to ensure cohesive engineering execution.
Oversee BOM integrity, approve critical build processes, and drive quality and cost engineering initiatives throughout the supply chain for your major assemblies.
Develop program schedules and partner with suppliers, quality, procurement, service, manufacturing, and engineering teams to drive complex open issues to closure and ensure on-time delivery.
Identify and communicate program progress, engineering challenges, and technical risks while proactively developing and leading strategic mitigation plans across the organization.
Lead the root-cause analysis and tracking of critical build and design issues impacting vehicle performance, quality, and production readiness to drive long-term engineering solutions.
Influence system designs to optimize performance, cost, quality, manufacturability, and serviceability by leading top-level design reviews, DFMEAs, validation programs, and manufacturing mock-builds.

B.S. or M.S. in Mechanical Engineering, Automotive Engineer, or a related technical discipline
12+ years of deep automotive engineering experience, with focus on Body, Closures or Chassis design and project management.

The Ads & Monetization organization sits at the heart of Pinterest’s business, where machine learning, AI, creatives, attribution, reach, and marketplace come together to create value for advertisers and relevant, inspiring experiences for Pinners.
Pinterest is at an inflection point. Hundreds of millions of users come to the platform with active commercial intent — making Pinterest uniquely positioned to influence the full purchase journey from inspiration to action.

We are building a path of non-linear growth with emerging surfaces, expanding international markets, and foundational investments in relevance, advertiser return on ads spend, measurement, and creative quality.

Unlocking that path requires disciplined, technically sophisticated execution across a collaborative, multi-team environment spanning technology, strategy, go-to-market and research.
As a Sr. Staff Technical Program Manager aligned to one of our monetization verticals such as ads or data science, you will use your technical depth and business judgment to lead company-level programs that turn these opportunities into measurable reality.

You will help shape the execution strategy, accountability frameworks, and operating models that determine how Pinterest scales its advertising business in a highly competitive and rapidly evolving market. This is one of the most senior individual contributor TPM roles in the Monetization organization, with direct impact on multiple company OKRs.

Lead company-level programs within Ads & Monetization — including areas such as Auction & Marketplace, Measurement & Attribution, Formats, and new surfaces — with direct impact on multiple company OKRs.
Identify opportunities to drive long-term business innovation and differentiation within Ads; anticipate business, technical, and regulatory issues that impact Pinterest’s monetization strategy.
Influence at the VP level: provide strategic input to leadership decision-making, drive alignment across orgs, and lead through technical credibility and communication — not through a management hierarchy.
Drive alignment across Product, Engineering, Data Science, Design, and Go-to-Market teams to deliver complex, vague, and strategically important Ads programs.
Own the metrics and accountability framework for your programs: connect delivery, performance, experimentation, and measurement signals into a clear source of truth for what shipped, what moved the metrics, and why.
Bring structure and decision velocity to ambiguous, high-stakes work by establishing decision frameworks, surfacing tradeoffs, managing dependencies, and increasing alignment speed across executive and cross-functional teams.
Exercise technical judgment equivalent to an L16 SWE: evaluate complex technical approaches, anticipate failure modes, sequence risky elements to fail fast, and guide teams in solving complex technical challenges across orgs.
Embed AI tools into program workflows to accelerate synthesis, planning, reporting, and repeatable workflows, applying appropriate judgment, verification, and privacy guardrails.
Provide thought leadership and mentorship: share best practices, create reusable tools and methodologies for the broader TPM org, and mentor PgMs and ICs across the company.

Minimum of 10 years of experience in technical program management or related experience leading company-level programs that directly impact business-critical objectives and revenue.
Demonstrated experience leading large-scale programs in ads, marketplace systems, machine learning/AI, ranking, recommendation systems, experimentation, measurement, data platforms, or similarly complex technical domains.
Track record of influencing senior leaders (VP/SVP/estaff) and aligning multiple organizations on programs of notable risk, complexity, and ambiguity.
Experience contributing to product or technology roadmaps at the company level, translating ambiguous business opportunities into clear priorities, measurable outcomes, and durable execution plans.
Expertise in building accountability systems across teams without a formal management structure: metric frameworks, roadmap tracking, launch governance, dependency management, and executive-level reporting.
Technical judgment and communication skills that allow you to guide engineering teams through complex tradeoffs, anticipate risks, and evaluate technical approaches without being the primary designer.
Demonstrated experience using AI to improve speed and quality in day-to-day program work, with a clear approach to validating accuracy, protecting sensitive data, and maintaining accountability for final decisions.
BS in Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science, or equivalent work experience.

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets - we're building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft and precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, including solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, and more.
Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration and in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S.

Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or vertically integrated components that help missions get to space, our world-class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions
SENIOR TECHNICAL PROGRAM MANAGER, SPACE SENSING & DOMAIN AWARENRESS (TS/SCI)
Based at Rocket Lab's global headquarters in Long Beach, CA, you are the program authority for our advanced optical and infrared sensing payloads. You own the technical roadmap and strategic “Make/Buy” decisions from the first “blank sheet” prototype, through flight qualification, and into scalable production.

This is a high-ownership role: you'll immerse yourself in the operational realities of the tracking, warning, and surveillance mission to turn their hardest problems into concrete technical milestones, and you'll be the person the program runs on.

Command the Lifecycle: Build and lead the team that takes EO/IR sensing payloads and optical systems from a “blank sheet” concept through qualification, scalable production, and flight, and own the technical roadmap that grows the team's core capabilities.
Lead the Team of Teams: Run multiple active programs at once, make sound architectural calls with Chief Engineers, navigate the hardest trade-offs in pointing stability and jitter, sensitivity, and revisit, and personally dive into the most program-threatening problems alongside the team.
Build the Bench: Grow a culture where strong people take smart, healthy risks and the best idea wins, no matter who it comes from, we back bold calls and treat an intelligent miss as the cost of moving fast, and coach and develop the next generation of program and team leaders.
Forge the Supply Chain: Manage high-stakes subcontracts and suppliers as strategic partners essential to the mission, protecting schedule and margin.
Unblock Excellence: Synchronize cross-functional teams across optics, electronics, software, and the data chain and clear roadblocks quickly so the team keeps moving at speed and quality stays high.
Influence the Future: Serve as the primary point of contact for assigned U.S. Government tracking, warning, and surveillance customers, and partner with BD & Strategy on proposals and technical narratives that define the next generation of space domain awareness.

Bachelor’s degree in physics, math, science, or other technical discipline
8+ years of aerospace program management experience
A demonstrated track record of owning a technical program, product, or team end to end and carrying it across the finish line under real pressure, we hire on what you've shipped, not years logged
Evidence you've moved real hardware and software from prototype toward scalable, flight-ready production
Understanding of the nuances of EO/IR sensing, optical payloads, or focal plane arrays
Experience identifying technical, schedule, or supply-chain risk and neutralizing it before it impacts the mission
Active TS/SCI clearance

Depth of Reps: Multiple program cycles or 8+ years in aerospace/defense, sharpen the edge, but we weight the hardest thing you've shipped over the count.

We are seeking a highly skilled Principal Technical Program Manager (TPM) to lead large, complex, cross-functional engineering programs supporting Public Sector. This is a senior individual-contributor role requiring strong technical depth, strategic program leadership, and the ability to communicate clearly at the VP/SVP/EVP level.

The Principal TPM must maintain working fluency in cloud architecture, distributed systems design, large-scale enterprise integration patterns, data flows, APIs/services, network engineering fundamentals, security, reliability, and modern SDLC/DevOps practices.

The Principal TPM converts business strategy into predictable engineering delivery, drives cross-value-stream alignment, manages critical dependencies and risks, and ensures executive stakeholders receive concise, decision-ready updates.

Location
This is a remote opportunity for candidates located anywhere in the U.S.

Lead the end-to-end lifecycle of large, complex, multi-team engineering programs, ensuring program structure, delivery rhythms, and engineering outcomes are clear and predictable.
Define and track performance metrics tied to engineering execution, program health, and SLAs with business and product stakeholders.
Develop and maintain engineering-aligned roadmaps, integrated timelines, dependency maps, budgets, and risk mitigation plans.
Build and lead program governance for executives, synthesizing engineering progress, risks, and technical trade-offs into clear, decision-oriented updates.
Implement best practices in engineering program governance, dependency management, cross-team risk visibility, SDLC alignment, and change management.
Foster a culture of accountability, technical excellence, and delivery predictability across engineering teams and partner groups.
Partner with finance, engineering, and product to monitor capital/opex, capacity utilization, and resource allocation across internal teams and vendors.
Report on program status including engineering risks, dependencies, integration concerns, and mitigation paths to senior leadership and key stakeholders.
Coordinate engineering planning cycles (roadmap planning, PI planning, quarterly commitments) and ensure backlogs are prioritized, estimated, and aligned with program objectives.
Contribute to strategic planning and partner across Product, Engineering, Architecture, and Operations to ensure engineering readiness for launches and major releases.

What We Look For in a Candidate

Bachelor’s degree in a technical field or equivalent experience; advanced degree is a plus.
12–15+ years of experience leading large-scale technical or engineering programs within complex, matrixed technology organizations.
Strong technical fluency in architecture, system design, APIs/services, data flows, and SDLC/DevOps.
Proven ability to communicate clearly and influence at the VP/SVP/EVP level—distilling complex engineering issues, risks, and trade-offs into concise recommendations.
Demonstrated experience managing engineering dependencies, sequencing across multiple teams, and driving outcomes across software and/or network domains.
Strong ability to navigate ambiguity, resolve cross-team conflicts, and turn strategy into structured engineering execution plans.
Exceptional stakeholder engagement and relationship-building skills across Product, Engineering, Architecture, Operations, and Finance.
High urgency, accountability, and operational rigor; sets high standards for clarity, delivery predictability, and tooling hygiene. PMP/PMI, Agile/SAFe, or Lean Six Sigma certifications are a plus.

s.h: Public Sector & Federal Compliance Experience Preferred

Experience leading or supporting large-scale Public Sector programs serving Federal, DoW, or other regulated government customers.
Working knowledge of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS), and their impact on technology delivery, cybersecurity, and contractual obligations.
Familiarity with federal cybersecurity and compliance frameworks, including FedRAMP, CMMC, FISMA, and applicable NIST publications (e.g., NIST SP 800-53 and NIST SP 800-171).
Understanding of Federal Contract Information (FCI), Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), and associated security, privacy, and data handling requirements.
Ability to translate regulatory, contractual, and cybersecurity requirements into executable program plans, risk management strategies, and executive-level communications.

You'll lead a lean, high-leverage team and take real ownership of both.

Build and lead the Marketing PMO Team
Mature the PMO into a full governance function: Building on the project and program management foundation already in place, operationalize the intake process, portfolio taxonomy, status rhythms and escalation protocols that bring Pinterest's full marketing project portfolio under one consistent operating system, covering flagship events, annual initiatives, international campaigns and regional activations.

Govern the marketing events portfolio: Own the project management infrastructure for Pinterest's marketing events. Embed project managers as independent trackers and escalation owners, not project stakeholders. Your team ensures milestones hold, risks surface early and blockers are cleared, while marketers and event leads own the creative and strategic work.
Own governance, not delivery: Position the PMO as a neutral party. Marketers own the work; the PMO owns the system that keeps it moving. Build a culture where rigor is a service, not a constraint.
Lead portfolio prioritization with business management: Model capacity against demand and equip VP and C-suite sponsors with the analysis needed for clear resource decisions. Operate as a credible planning partner to Finance, serving as a neutral lens on portfolio health and trade-offs.

You'll determine what belongs in the stack, make the build/buy/integrate calls, and bring these capabilities online in a way that's secure, scalable and connected to Pinterest's existing systems. This will all be in partnership with our marketing technical teams.
Set the quality bar for technology outputs: The team owns what the tools produce. Establish the review cadence, accuracy thresholds and escalation triggers that ensure automated outputs meet the standard before they reach senior stakeholders. You are accountable for the integrity of the full PMO output, both human and AI-generated.
Evolve the stack as the function matures: As the PMO's operating model develops, continuously assess what the technology can take on, where it needs improvement and where human judgment remains essential. Make that line explicit and hold both sides of it accountable.

We are seeking a Principal Technical Program Manager to join our APEX Strategic Programs organization. In this role, you will drive ServiceNow's most critical cross-functional priorities and strategic programs— operating at the intersection of strategy and execution and setting the standard for how high-impact programs are designed, governed, and run at scale.
This person will operate as an AI-native leader, using AI tools to accelerate program delivery, synthesize intelligence across workstreams and model the ways of working we expect to scale across APEX. This candidate thinks strategically but loves getting into the details and possesses a strong ability to conceptualize, develop, drive, coordinate and manage large, complex, cross-functional programs supporting formal company Objectives and Key Results (OKRs).

We are looking for a Technical Program Manager to own the operational readiness and ongoing health of our fleet of Data Centers, both COLO and BTS sites.

In this role you will be the single point of accountability for ensuring each site runs as expected — SLAs met, maintenance executed on schedule, and audits passed — across a growing portfolio of landlord-operated and purpose-built facilities.

You will operate as the primary interface between Nebius and our data center landlords and operators, and you will partner closely with the Nebius IT team to translate site-level operations into reliable infrastructure for our customers.

Own the operational health of Nebius COLO and BTS sites, ensuring each facility runs to expectation across power, cooling, space, connectivity, security, and environmental controls.
Track, monitor, and enforce SLA compliance across landlords and colocation providers; identify breaches, drive remediation, and hold providers accountable to contractual commitments.
Manage and coordinate site maintenance schedules — preventive and corrective — including planning and approving maintenance windows, reviewing Methods of Procedure (MOPs), and minimizing risk to live workloads.
Plan and drive site audits covering compliance, capacity, power/cooling performance, physical security, and safety; track findings to closure.
Serve as the primary day-to-day interface with data center landlords and operators, managing the operational relationship, escalations, and coordination of on-site activity.

Build reporting mechanisms and dashboards that give leadership clear visibility into site health, SLA performance, maintenance status, and open risk across the portfolio.
Lead incident coordination and post-incident follow-up, including root cause analysis and corrective action tracking with landlords and internal teams.
Track and manage contractual operational obligations, deliverables, and timelines across multiple sites and providers simultaneously.

We are seeking a Senior Technical Program Manager to own our vulnerability management program end to end.

In this role, you will drive vulnerability intake, triage, remediation, and reporting across our bug bounty program, our Google Cloud Platform (GCP) infrastructure, source code hosted on GitHub, and a broad portfolio of third-party SaaS services.

You will partner closely with platform engineering, product engineering, SRE, security, IT, legal, and vendor management to make sure vulnerabilities are found fast, triaged accurately, and closed within SLA — and that leadership always has a clear, current picture of the organization's risk posture.The ideal candidate uses AI and automation aggressively to scale themselves, but understands that the core value is clarity, tradeoffs, and execution, not just tooling.

Program Ownership: Own and continuously improve the vulnerability management program, including intake, severity scoring (CVSS/risk-based), SLA definition, and remediation tracking across all asset types.
Bug Bounty Operations: Manage the triage/payouts/rewards workflow, and report on program health and trends.
Cloud Remediation (GCP): Drive remediation of vulnerabilities found in GCP infrastructure — IAM, networking, Compute/GKE, storage, and logging/monitoring configuration — by partnering with security, cloud, and platform engineering teams.
Code & Supply Chain Security: Coordinate remediation of vulnerabilities surfaced through SAST/DAST/SCA tooling (Wiz Code, Snyk, Dependabot, code scanning, secret scanning) across engineering repos, including dependency and supply-chain risk.
SaaS Vendor Risk: Build and manage the process for assessing and tracking security posture across third-party SaaS applications.
Escalation & Exceptions: Define and enforce escalation paths for overdue or critical/high-severity findings, including risk acceptance and exception processes with appropriate sign-off.
Cross-Team Accountability: Partner with engineering managers and tech leads to embed remediation work into sprint planning and hold teams accountable to remediation SLAs.
Reporting & Alerting: Establish and maintain a single source of truth for vulnerability status, aging, SLA compliance, and risk trends, with dashboards for engineering leadership, security leadership, and executives.
Audit & Compliance Support: Support audit and compliance efforts (SOC 2, ISO 27001, customer security questionnaires) by keeping vulnerability management evidence and metrics audit-ready.
Process & Automation: Drive process improvements and automation to reduce manual triage effort and improve time-to-remediation across all vulnerability sources.

Experience: 4–6+ years of experience in technical program management, security program management, or security operations, with direct ownership of a vulnerability management or application security program.
Bug Bounty Expertise: Hands-on experience running a bug bounty program (e.g., HackerOne, Bugcrowd, Intigriti), including triage and payout workflows.
Cloud Security Knowledge (GCP): Working knowledge of GCP security fundamentals: IAM, VPC/networking, Security Command Center, Cloud Logging/Monitoring, and common cloud misconfiguration risks.
Code Security Familiarity: Familiarity with GitHub-based development workflows and code security tooling (Wiz Code, Dependabot, SAST/DAST/SCA tools such as Snyk, Semgrep, or CodeQL).
Risk Prioritization: Strong grasp of vulnerability scoring frameworks (CVSS) and risk-based prioritization.
Communication: Excellent cross-functional communication skills — able to translate technical vulnerability data into business risk for executive audiences and hold engineering teams accountable without owning the code themselves.
Reporting Tools: Proven ability to build reporting/dashboards (e.g., Linear, Jira, ServiceNow, Tableau, Looker) that give leadership real-time visibility into program health.
Compliance Awareness: Experience supporting compliance frameworks such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI-DSS, or FedRAMP.

Systems Thinking: The ability to see the “big picture” and understand how vulnerability management decisions impact the entire stack — cloud, code, and vendor ecosystem alike.
Technical Influence: The ability to drive alignment across engineering and security through expertise and collaboration rather than direct authority.
Autonomy: Comfortable owning a program end to end and driving outcomes with minimal oversight.
Bias for Action: A track record of closing the gap between finding a vulnerability and actually getting it fixed.

Margins 2 Markets (M2M) is building key components of an effective waste management system in three ecologically valuable coastal regions: Raja Ampat/Sorong (Indonesia), Tamil Nadu (India), and Zanzibar (Tanzania).

These regions face similar challenges: remote and growing coastal communities, insufficient waste management infrastructure, limited access to recycling markets, and increasing plastic pollution from tourism and population growth, driving marine litter and threatening biodiversity, fisheries, and local livelihoods.
The project establishes regional collection, pre-processing, and recycling infrastructure, including Material Recovery Facilities (MRFs) and pre-processing sites, and connects these to national and international recycling markets.

It combines this physical infrastructure with digital traceability systems, incentive schemes for waste collectors, training, occupational health and safety measures, and transparent payment systems.

The overarching goal is to prevent approximately 40,000 tonnes of plastic waste from entering coastal and marine ecosystems and to develop a replicable model for other coastal regions.

A regional MRF in Ramanathapuram, Tamil Nadu, cleaning, sorting, and baling fishing nets and marine plastics, alongside collection activities across 14 coastal districts.
Pre-processing facilities near Kendwa and Paje (Zanzibar) plus a central MRF between Zanzibar City and the landfill.
Local collection and pre-processing sites across the Raja Ampat islands, linked to a central facility in Sorong.

SoSafe has the ambition to become the leading human risk management provider in Europe. Our award-winning awareness platform triggers behavioural change by providing effective and engaging training and simulations on cybersecurity and data protection. Cybercrime is costing the world >$10 trillion annually and growing by 15% p.a. - we invite you to be part of the solution!

Platform work at SoSafe carries outsized leverage. One well-run migration touches a dozen services at once. One adopted shared library saves every team that builds on it from solving the same problem twice. One monitoring signal catches a problem before a customer ever sees it. The work often goes unnoticed when it's going well, but its absence is felt across half of Product Development within a week.
We're hiring a Technical Program Manager to embed into one of our platform teams and bring order to that complexity. You'll partner closely with the Product Manager, Engineering Manager, and their Tech Leads to drive the when and how of the roadmap: sequencing the work, surfacing risk early, holding cross-team commitments together, and making sure what ships lands cleanly across every team that depends on it.
This role owns program outcomes, not status reports. You'll think in systems, work in mechanisms, and earn trust by removing friction the team didn't know was costing them time.
Here's how you'll make a difference
Own end-to-end delivery for programs that touch a dozen services at once: an architecture migration, a compliance remediation, a legacy system sunset.
Partner with Product Management and GTM stakeholders on platform changes with customer-facing impact, keeping rollouts, communications, and external commitments in lockstep with engineering delivery.
Drive adoption of shared platform capabilities that other teams are supposed to build on, closing the gap between "we shipped it" and teams actually using it.
Manage multi-team migrations where downstream consumers, external commitments, and legacy constraints all need to land in the right order. A missed dependency here costs months, not days.
Run the mechanics that keep a dozen concurrent programs honest: dependency maps, risk logs, decision records, and the recurring check-ins nobody wants to run but everybody needs.
Bring rigor to how delivery health gets measured, incident counts, adoption rates, time-to-land, and use it to drive change instead of producing another report.
What makes you a great fit
You've run complex, cross-functional technical programs and can point to ones where the technical decisions were yours to shape, not just to track.
You hold your own in deep engineering conversations. You don't need to write the code, but you need to understand what's being argued about and why it matters.
You bring structure to ambiguity without over-engineering it. Your default is the lightest mechanism that solves the problem.
You've worked where the consumers of your output are other engineering teams, whether that's infrastructure, data pipelines, or internal APIs.
You've managed a migration or sunset with real downstream impact, and you know how to land it without breaking trust.
You communicate directly. Short sentences, clear asks, no filler. You write decisions down and make sure the right people see them.
You're comfortable in Jira, Confluence, and the rest of a modern engineering toolchain, and you have opinions about how they should be used.

Background in infrastructure, data engineering, or applied AI/ML platforms.
Experience inside a SaaS company through a phase of platform consolidation or modernization.
Familiarity with SLOs or monitoring practice as a delivery signal, not just an SRE artifact.
What success looks like
3 months. You're embedded with the team's engineering leadership, have a clear read on every active program, and have started reshaping how the group plans, tracks, and communicates delivery.
6 months. You're the trusted operating partner for the group. Initiatives that were drifting are landing predictably, and the cross-team dependencies that used to surprise us are surfacing weeks earlier.
12 months. The team is delivering with a rhythm other groups want to copy. The mechanisms you built are running themselves, and you're picking the next compounding problem to solve.

About LILT
AI is changing how the world communicates — and LILT is leading that transformation.
We're on a mission to make the world's information accessible to everyone , regardless of the language they speak. We use cutting-edge AI, machine translation, and human-in-the-loop expertise to translate content faster, more accurately, and more cost-effectively without compromising on brand, voice, or quality.
At LILT, we empower our teammates with leading tools, global collaboration, and growth opportunities to do their best work. Our company virtues— Work together, win together; Find a way or make one; Quicker than they expect; Quality is Job 1 —guide everything we do.

We are trusted by Intel Corporation , Canva , the United States Department of Defense , the United States Air Force , ASICS , and hundreds of global Enterprises. Backed by Sequoia, Intel Capital, and Redpoint, we’re building a category-defining company in a $50B+ global translation market being redefined by AI.

As a Senior TPM of Applied AI, you will sit at the intersection of cutting-edge research and industrial-scale execution. You will operate with an entrepreneurial mindset, effectively acting as the CEO of your customer's business to proactively drive success. You are responsible for leading complex benchmark transformations and data deliverables.

Rather than just managing timelines, you are architecting workflows to ensure the next generation of LLMs and multimodal models are trained on the most accurate, diverse, and complex data available, while championing innovative solutions alongside our research lab partners.
Entrepreneurial Benchmark Leadership: Act as the CEO of your customer’s business by proactively proposing and co-developing benchmark transcreations directly with research lab partners, ensuring our deliverables are innovative, tailored, and aligned with their core research objectives.
Frontier Lab Program Management: Lead the end-to-end execution of high-priority technical programs for frontier AI labs, managing the delivery of massive-scale datasets and bespoke engineering milestones.
High-Volume Data Operations: Architect and oversee pipelines for delivering high-volume data samples across multiple modalities (text, image, video, audio), ensuring strict adherence to delivery cadences without sacrificing precision.
End-to-End Quality Control: Partner with production to implement rigorous, automated, and human-in-the-loop QC frameworks to ensure data integrity across various domains and languages.
Cross-Functional Leadership: Bridge the gap between forward-deployed engineering resources, research, and production teams to ensure LILT can serve the needs of the frontier AI market.

Education: B.S or M.S. in Computer Science, AI, or a related technical field with 10+ years of industry experience. Equivalently, a Ph.D. with 5+ years of experience in a high-growth AI/Engineering environment.
Entrepreneurial Mindset: Experience founding or scaling a venture, or operating in an early-stage startup environment where you drove business growth and strategic initiatives from the ground up.
Strategic Execution: Strong business acumen and the ability to manage high-stakes stakeholder relationships with frontier AI labs.
Frontier AI Expertise: Proven track record of managing data pipelines for LLMs or multimodal models. Deep understanding of training, inference, and the nuances of data diversity (multilingual and multi-domain).
Scale & Quality: Demonstrated ability to manage "high-throughput" programs where quality control is mission-critical. You should have experience with automated validation at scale.

Our Story
Our founders, Spence and John met at Google working on Google Translate. As researchers at Stanford and Berkeley, they both worked on language technology to make information accessible to everyone. While together at Google, they were amazed to learn that Google Translate wasn’t used for enterprise products and services inside the company.The quality just wasn’t there. So they set out to build something better. LILT was born.
LILT has been a machine learning company since its founding in 2015. At the time, machine translation didn’t meet the quality standard for enterprise translations, so LILT assembled a cutting-edge research team tasked with closing that gap. While meeting customer demand for translation services, LILT has prioritized investments in Large Language Models, human-in-the-loop systems, and now agentic AI.
With AI innovation accelerating and enterprise demand growing, the next phase of LILT’s journey is just beginning.
