Own the operating model. Design and run the Lab's core processes from the ground up: portfolio management, roadmap tracking, async documentation, and decision-making cadence. Where a task recurs, build a process.
Connect research and product. Understand both the Lab's projects and product teams' roadmaps well enough to propose concrete collaborations and follow them through. Lead recurring interfaces such as the bi-annual DS-Research workshop and monthly research on-sites, with agendas set in advance and pre-reads produced and read before the meeting.
Filter and triage inbound. Manage partnership proposals, collaboration requests, and internal asks: answering or redirecting most, escalating only what merits researcher time.
Track dependencies to resolution. Own operational blockers (data access, compute, contracts, academic collaboration administration) and drive them to closure with the relevant teams. For example: run a CIFRE application through the university, the doctoral school, and the ANRT fast enough that the intern starts the PhD without a gap.
Run hiring logistics. Interface with Talent Acquisition to keep the pipeline moving: scheduling, candidate communication, process documentation, scorecard templates. Researchers keep the assessments.
Map the ecosystem. Maintain a live view of labs, companies, and institutions working on adjacent topics; prepare targeting decisions for partnerships, workshops, and data challenges. Lead the first data challenge end to end, from platform setup and legal clearance to participant communication.
Move information in both directions. Collect what the Lab needs from product, data, medical, legal, and people teams; report the Lab's scientific outputs, programme health, and critical risks to the company with clarity and precision.
Before you read on: if you don't have the exact profile described below but feel this job description matches your skill set, we still encourage you to apply.

s.h: You'll be a great fit if you
s.t:
Have at least 5 years of experience in programme management, research operations, or a comparable high-complexity role, ideally within an AI, engineering, scientific, or product environment
Have a demonstrated ability to design and run processes from scratch, coordinate multiple workstreams across specialist teams, and hold a portfolio of priorities, dependencies, risks, and milestones with rigour
Are able to influence senior stakeholders and expert teams without formal authority, and follow unresolved items until they are resolved
Communicate with clarity and economy: you can make complex topics actionable for non-technical audiences and precise for technical ones
Have enough understanding of machine learning to follow research discussions, judge which requests merit researcher time, and translate the team's goals for the rest of the company; deep domain expertise can be learned on the job
Are fluent in English; working French is required, as academic-administration processes (CIFRE, ANRT, doctoral schools) run in French

s.h: It would be fantastic if you
s.t:
Have operated as Chief of Staff to a CTO, VP Engineering, Research Director, or Head of AI, or as a Research Operations Manager in an AI lab, university, hospital, or industrial research organisation
Are familiar with academic-industry collaborations, CIFRE, PhD programmes, grants, or data challenges
Have experience with clinical AI, healthtech, model evaluation, AI safety, privacy, or data governance

### Who We Are ###
We are the Process and Tooling team supporting CIA Network Fiber, focused on simplifying how teams plan, source, deliver, and manage fiber work across regions. Our team partners closely with sourcing, delivery, engineering, operations, GIS, and regional stakeholders to turn complex workflows into clear, scalable processes and practical tooling solutions.

Our mission is to create consistent, efficient, and repeatable ways of working that reduce manual effort, improve visibility, and help teams move fiber programs forward with greater speed and confidence. We focus on standardizing processes, improving tool adoption, clarifying ownership, and enabling better decision-making through reliable data and well-defined workflows.

We are seeking a Technical Program Manager to drive process & tooling optimization and automation, primarily focused on AI driven improvements to accelerate transformation across global cloud and network operations.
This role sits at the intersection of business process optimization, AI adoption, tooling, and intelligent automation engineering. You will lead the identification, development, and scaling of AI powered capabilities, process improvement and tooling requirements -embedding Copilot, automation, and predictive analytics into operational workflows to improve speed to market, data quality, cost efficiency, and decision making.
The ideal candidate thrives in complex, matrixed environments, can move seamlessly between strategy and execution, and delivers measurable impact through responsible, scalable AI solutions.
**Key Responsibilities - Process Optimization, Tooling & Automation with Focus on AI**
* Map, analyze, and optimize end-to-end operational processes across network sourcing, inventory, planning, fiber lifecycle, and engineering workflows.
* Eliminate friction, standardize practices, and reduce cycle times using AI enabled automation.
* Partner with CIA and our partner teams to ensure integrated, scalable tooling solutions aligned to business priorities.
**AI, Data & System Integration**
* Strengthen data quality, interoperability, and automation across network and operational tools.
* Enable AI powered data cleansing, reconciliation, forecasting, and predictive modeling.
* Support system modernization initiatives to ensure platforms are AI-ready and interoperable.
* Act as a connector between business owners, engineering teams, and AI/data science resources.
* Design, develop, and deploy agents and agent flows that support operational workflows.
* Translate repeatable patterns into scalable, automated solutions.
* Ensure AI solutions are reliable, maintainable, secure, and aligned with engineering best practices.
* Integrate automation solutions with existing systems and Microsoft platforms.
* Support deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement of AI and automation solutions in production environments.
* Contribute to technical documentation, operational readiness, and knowledge sharing.
* Lead AI change management efforts to drive AI literacy and adoption across teams.
* Develop training, documentation, and communications that accelerate responsible AI usage.
* Foster an AI first, growth mindset culture grounded in Microsoft-s Responsible AI principles, security, and governance standards.

* Bachelor-s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data, Telecommunications, Finance, or related field AND some experience in these fields OR equivalent experience
* Some experience managing cross-functional and/or cross-team projects

* Some experience in cloud, data center, or large-scale network environments.
* Solid experience in program management, process improvement, automation, or operations.

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

Rocket Lab’s Space Systems division builds complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space including solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, and radios.
The Space Systems division has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help get to space — our Space Systems division is empowering the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

Our vision is to revolutionize the space-based payload market with innovative and novel designs for space, terrestrial, and airborne environments.

Team & Role
Moveworks, now part of ServiceNow, is building the agentic AI layer that sits between every employee and the systems they rely on. Following the acquisition, the Moveworks Business Unit is one of the most strategically important investments at ServiceNow — and the scope of what we own is expanding fast.

We are looking for a Director-level Technical Program Manager (Individual Contributor) to lead our most critical programs end to end, starting with the ServiceNow integration and growing into a broader portfolio over time as the BU scales.
This is a senior, highly technical IC role for someone who has spent most of their career running infrastructure, platform modernization, or large-scale distributed systems programs. You will manage the program — directly, end to end — and your influence will come from technical depth, sharp judgment, and an ability to align engineering leaders, executives, and partner organizations around a single execution plan. As the Moveworks BU scope expands, so will yours.

s.h: What you get to do in this role
s.t:
Own the Moveworks Infrastructure portfolio of strategic and technical initiatives. Your primary focus will be to drive the roadmap and execution plans for Moveworks Infrastructure initiatives; as you scale you will also take over from engineering infra operational processes like capacity planning and budgeting
Focus on initiatives expanding MW Infra footprint . We are moving to a tri-cloud + on-prem + SPC strategy where we need to develop the tools and process for managing our infra stack across diverse environments. Align any ambiguous strategic direction into concrete milestones, dependencies, and decision points.
Run the program, not the people . As the TPM, you will be the connective tissue across engineering, product, design, security, GTM, finance, and field organizations — driving outcomes through clarity, structured decision-making, and relentless follow-through.
Identify and resolve technical misalignment . Spot misalignment across teams, architectures, and roadmaps early — before it becomes a delivery risk — and partner with engineering leads to drive resolution quickly. Lead architecture reviews, surface cross-system risks (latency budgets, blast radius, multi-tenancy, AI safety, evals), and broker tradeoffs between engineering teams.
Build the operating system for the program . Status, risk, scope, and decision logs that engineering directors and VPs actually read. Quarterly planning rhythms that reflect reality. Executive narratives that are honest about where things stand.
Be the senior partner to engineering leadership . Pair directly with Distinguished Engineers, VPs of Engineering, and product leaders. Represent the program to the CTO, CPO, and executive staff. Own the message.
Define TPM excellence . As we grow and expand our TPM team, you will serve as the model for how to operate. Set the standard for what senior technical program management looks like at Moveworks, mentor TPMs across the org without being their manager, and codify the patterns that scale.

12+ years of technical program management experience, with most of that time spent on infrastructure, platform, cloud, reliability, developer productivity, or modernization programs. You have operated at staff, principal, or director IC scope on programs where the hard part was not coordination alone, but understanding technical dependencies, sequencing migrations, managing reliability risk, and helping engineering leaders make durable tradeoffs.
Deep technical fluency across infrastructure modernization domains — distributed systems, cloud-native infrastructure, Kubernetes, multi-region and multi-cloud architectures, hyperscaler platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP), identity, data platforms, observability, reliability, and migration strategy. You do not need to be the architect, but you need enough technical depth to pressure-test plans, spot cross-system risk, and earn credibility with senior engineers.
A track record of leading cross-org programs involving 100+ engineers, multiple VPs, and competing roadmaps — ideally including at least one large-scale integration, migration, or platform unification.
Excellent written communication. You can compress a 200-engineer program into a one-page exec narrative without losing the truth of it. You write decision docs that hold up under scrutiny.
Strong technical judgment under ambiguity. You know when to dig in, when to delegate to engineering leads, and when to escalate. You are comfortable saying “this plan won’t work” in a room full of senior leaders.

Prior IC senior TPM experience at a hyperscaler, large SaaS platform, or AI-first company.
Comfort operating across SaaS, on-prem regulated, and government cloud (FedRAMP, IL5) deployment models.
Experience leading post-acquisition technical integration programs at scale.
Background in agentic AI, conversational AI, or AI assistant platforms — you understand why agent runtimes, tool calling, RAG, and evals are not the same problem.

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.
Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.
We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

Airbnb’s mission is to create a world where people can Belong Anywhere. As we grow to achieve that mission, we’re looking to add a technical, hands-on, and mission-driven Technical Program Manager (TPM) for the Payments team.
A person in this role will partner with our Payments organization to provide a cohesive set of technology offerings that enable everything related to moving money in Airbnb’s global marketplace - moving billions of dollars, in 191 countries, across 75 currencies, through a complex ecosystem of payments partners.

Within Payments Tech, we have Payments Platform, Compliance & Operations, Payments Engineering Services, and Payments Data Engineering. These programs work together to deliver reliable systems that allow guests and Hosts to make and receive payments with clarity and ease.

As our payments platform grows we’ll be adding new payment partners, global licenses, compliance and regulation controls, and building new payment experiences for our guests and hosts.
This role is deeply cross-organization, as projects will span across a wide surface area, and building positive relationships across a multitude of technical teams will be essential to the success of this leader.

We are looking for candidates who share our passion for tackling complexity head-on while supporting and growing a world class team of Technical Program Managers.

In addition to helping their team deliver predictable, consistent program execution, this leader should have a strong sense of ownership and ability to think and work strategically with a variety of stakeholders.

TPMs at Airbnb work on a variety of complex projects/ programs that touch multiple services, functions and teams, and hence are required to keep the big picture in focus while being
able to dive into the details, working through unique challenges we face daily. They're good at building relationships, motivating others with vision, and persuading with data. It is a highly leveraged role that aims to improve the quality and velocity of work across cross-functional teams by acting as a “force multiplier”.

This includes managing project schedules, identifying risks, discussing the technical trade-offs with engineers, and maintaining clear communications across multiple stakeholder groups across the organization. In short, they get things done by bringing clarity out of chaos, diving into the details, and communicating clearly and in a timely manner.
A Typical Day
Develop program scope and objectives, collaborate with all relevant stakeholders, ensure technical feasibility and drive projects end-to-end.
Align on staffing, priorities and technical dependencies within Hosting and cross-functional teams like Trust, Payments, Infra & Product both in terms of quarterly planning, and managing ongoing risk escalation/ mitigation.
Manage Technical Design diligence process for large programs, track technical dependencies, scheduling reviews and pre-reviews, engaging the right stakeholders across teams, and managing meeting quality and efficiency.
Manage effective communications to leadership and across teams on key decisions, status, and risks to ensure accountability and timeline management.
Understand best practices, drive for process improvements, and find new ways of operating, with a focus on simplification and productivity.
Drive org-wide and company-wide technical initiatives as we evolve our technical stack to scale for the next decade
Provide visibility into key performance indicators so leaders are aware of risks and opportunities.

About Phaidra
Phaidra is building the future of industrial automation.
The world today is filled with static, monolithic infrastructure. Factories, power plants, buildings, etc. operate the same they've operated for decades — because the controls programming is hard-coded. Thousands of lines of rules and heuristics that define how the machines interact with each other. The result of all this hard-coding is that facilities are frozen in time, unable to adapt to their environment while their performance slowly degrades.
Phaidra creates AI-powered control systems for the industrial sector, enabling industrial facilities to automatically learn and improve over time. Specifically:
We use reinforcement learning algorithms to provide this intelligence, converting raw sensor data into high-value actions and decisions.
We focus on industrial applications, which tend to be well-sensorized with measurable KPIs — perfect for reinforcement learning.
We enable domain experts (our users) to configure the AI control systems (i.e. agents) without writing code. They define what they want their AI agents to do, and we do it for them.
Our team has a track record of applying AI to some of the toughest problems. From achieving superhuman performance with DeepMind's AlphaGo, to reducing the energy required to cool Google's Data Centers by 40%, we deeply understand AI and how to apply it in production for massive impact.
Phaidra’s ability to achieve its mission is determined by our ability to work together — as defined by our core values: Agency, Velocity , Craft , and Truth . We seek individuals who embody these values, as they are instrumental in ensuring our team consistently delivers excellence and fosters an engaging and supportive culture
Phaidra is based in the USA, but we are 100% remote with no physical office. We hire employees internationally with the help of our partner, OysterHR. Our team is currently located throughout the USA, Canada, UK, Sweden, Spain, Portugal, the Netherlands, Singapore, Australia, and India.

You’re an independent worker, skilled in organization, planning, and project management.
You have technical knowledge of industrial controls, building automation systems, and/or air or water cooled chiller plants.
You have the drive to learn about different industries and technologies, and a passion to help customers operate their plant more efficiently and effectively with Phaidra’s AI supervisory control system.
You can take ownership of your assigned customers and delight them!
You can guide internal and external teams as you coordinate the configuration and installation of the customers industrial plant AI Agents, and provide professional support while you grow customer relationships for future expansion and advocacy.
You thrive in a process-driven environment, yet possess the flexibility to adapt and tailor those processes to each customer's unique needs.
You enjoy collaborating with cross-functional teams to tackle complex projects, leveraging your expertise to drive successful outcomes.

Spreedly is the world's leading Open Payments Platform. Founded in 2007 and headquartered in Durham, NC, the company gives mid-market and enterprise businesses the infrastructure to connect to any payment gateway, processor, or fraud tool through a single API. The platform is vendor-agnostic by design, meaning customers are never locked into a single provider and never need to rebuild their payments stack to access new capabilities.
The core business problem Spreedly solves is real and costly: global merchants face a fragmented payments ecosystem, where every new market, payment method, or fraud tool typically requires a separate, time-consuming integration. Spreedly eliminates that complexity, enabling companies to route transactions intelligently, secure cardholder data, prevent fraud, and expand into new markets without heavy engineering overhead.

As a Technical Program Manager , you will be a key player in our pre-sales and customer solutioning efforts. You will partner closely with Account Executives, Product, and Engineering to scope technical solutions that align with customer needs and drive Spreedly's growth. This is a customer-facing, consultative role focused on understanding prospect pain points and designing solutions that connect Spreedly's platform capabilities to business outcomes.
You will also influence revenue growth, shorten time-to-close, and accelerate value realization for our customers. As Spreedly scales, this role will shape our go-to-market infrastructure through solution templates, demo assets, and mentoring, making it an ideal opportunity for impact and professional growth.
This is a US-based customer-facing role supporting primarily US customers and cross-functional teams operating within US business hours. Success in this role requires regular travel within the United States and the ability to work in alignment with US customer and internal stakeholder schedules.

Additional Information

Spreedly provides an open payments platform. The platform’s connectivity provides payments performance. Key products and services include:
Connect — A unified API that integrates with hundreds of payment gateways, processors, and alternative payment methods worldwide, including digital wallets. Merchants access the global payments ecosystem through one connection.
Vault — A PCI-compliant secure repository for payment methods. Merchants store card data once and reuse it across any payment service, reducing PCI scope and protecting cardholder data at scale.
Optimize — Workflow-driven routing and retry logic that directs each transaction to the best-performing gateway in real time. On average, 7.9% of failed transactions succeed immediately when retried on a secondary gateway. This is where merchants recover lost revenue and increase authorization success rates.
Protect — A flexible fraud and authentication layer, incorporating advanced fraud tools and 3DS. Following Spreedly's acquisition of Dodgeball in September 2025, fraud orchestration and payment optimization now operate within the same platform.
Resolve — Centralized management and reporting that reduces operational silos, strengthens security, and improves billing control across a merchant's entire payment operation.

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

Claude is used across government, from US federal civilian agencies to national security, state and local, and allied international governments, and nearly every model and product Anthropic ships has public sector work on the end of it.

Each of those segments runs under its own regulatory and deployment constraints, so delivering Claude to them means standing up compliant infrastructure with cloud partners, landing new models in restricted environments, bringing our application suite to parity with commercial, and clearing frameworks like FedRAMP, repeated for every segment.

We're hiring a Technical Program Manager to own that program.
Today that coordination is spread across the public sector product and engineering leads and the many teams they pull in: research, infrastructure, security, compliance, and product engineering. You'll become the single owner of that program, the person who knows where every workstream stands, what it is waiting on, and who needs to decide.

Over time, government customers get new models and products on a predictable cadence, authorizations like FedRAMP run as a steady program rather than a one-off push, and each new segment takes less bespoke effort than the last.

Own the program for delivering new Claude models into public sector environments: sequencing, dependencies, and tradeoffs across research, inference and capacity, cloud partners, safeguards, and compliance teams
Drive FedRAMP and similar authorization programs for Anthropic's public sector offerings, working with privacy, security, compliance, and platform engineering
Plan and sequence work across public sector segments, from model and API availability to application parity and segment-specific product work
Represent public sector requirements in model launch planning alongside the launch TPMs
Establish the operating rhythm: a single view of workstreams, owners, dependencies, risks, and status, with planning, escalation paths, and launch coordination across orgs
Convert recurring efforts into documented, repeatable processes so that each new segment or model requires less bespoke coordination

Have several years of experience in technical program management, with a track record of successfully delivering complex, cross-functional programs
Have shipped software or infrastructure into regulated or restricted environments (government clouds, air-gapped deployments, FedRAMP or similar authorization frameworks) and can engage meaningfully with the infrastructure, ML, and security engineers doing the work
Have experience coordinating across multiple engineering teams and organizations simultaneously, including research, security, and compliance partners
Are highly organized and can manage multiple parallel workstreams effectively across distributed teams
Thrive in unstructured environments with a knack for bringing order to chaos and creating clarity in ambiguous situations
Have excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence without authority
Have worked on public sector, defense, or government cloud programs, or hold or are eligible for a US security clearance (preferred but not required)
Are passionate about Anthropic's mission and interested in the challenges of bringing AI capabilities to public institutions safely and reliably

How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles.

We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

As Director of Technical Program Management for Driver Out at Wayve, you'll own the multi-year program that takes Wayve's autonomy technology and operationalises it - from our first eyes-off, driver-out demonstration through to a productised, scaled service on public roads.

Driver Out is the underlying technology program behind Wayve's robotaxi ambitions: where the robotaxi pilots prove the product in different markets, you own the safety, systems, and delivery foundations that make driver-out real.
You'll lead an org-wide effort spanning driving-model performance and safety, behaviour validation, the safety case, system architecture, functional safety and V&V, vehicle hardware and software, remote assistance, and operations - turning a complex web of “must be true” conditions into a sequenced, credible plan.

You'll partner with engineering, science, safety, product, and operations leaders (and external partners such as OEMs and Uber), and build and lead the TPM team beneath the program. Your impact is measured in how safely and predictably Wayve moves from driver-in to driver-out.

A successful leader here is a force multiplier - creating clarity across a huge, ambiguous, safety-critical program.

Own the Driver Out program end-to-end: Define and drive the multi-year plan and milestones - from the first driver-out demonstration to public-road product integration and minimal scaling - from concept to operation.
Lead the program org: Build, coach, and grow the TPM team across the program; set the operating model and hold workstream leads to account.
Drive the critical path: Turn a complex set of “must be true” conditions into a sequenced plan; own dependencies, risk, and trade-offs across every workstream.
Own the safety-critical spine: Bring the safety case, behaviour validation, functional safety (ISO 26262), SOTIF (ISO 21448), cybersecurity, and the Safety Management System together into a credible, signed-off argument for driver-out.
Partner across the company and externally: Align engineering, science, safety, product, and operations - and external partners (OEMs, Uber) - on scope, sequencing, and readiness.
Establish scalable practices: Governance, milestone and launch-readiness reviews, KPIs and dashboards, escalations, and risk-budget management.
Represent Driver Out at the top: Report progress, risk, and readiness to the executive team, and steer the biggest calls.

The Supply Chain Programme Manager is a critical cross-functional role responsible for owning end-to-end supply chain execution across assigned programmes and product builds at Wayve. This includes prototype development, new product introduction (NPI), and supporting fleet launches.
This role serves as the primary Supply Chain lead ensuring meeting programme deliverables, supplier compliance, and seamless coordination across Engineering, Operations, Manufacturing, and external partners. The ideal candidate thrives in a fast-moving, hardware-driven environment and brings both strategic thinking and hands-on execution capability.
The role works cross-functionally with Engineering, Planning, Sourcing, Logistics, Finance, Legal, and Suppliers, and partners closely with global upfitters and third-party integration partners (spanning the US, UK, and other regions) to ensure vehicle and programme timelines are met.
Programme Ownership & Cross-Functional Coordination
Act as the primary Supply Chain lead for assigned programmes or internal product builds (e.g., prototypes, new product introduction, subassembly).
Own end-to-end material readiness to support programme milestones across R&D, Engineering, Operations, and Manufacturing.

Act as the strategic liaison between hardware engineering and the procurement teams, managing demand aggregation.
Material Planning & Readiness
Translate engineering BOMs and aggregate Technical Programme Manager demand into procurement plans
Identify long-lead items and critical path components early in the product lifecycle.
Track material status through build phases and escalate gaps or risks proactively.
Programme Managing Upfitter / Partner

Drive upfitter/partner activities to ensure vehicles meet overall programme timelines and quality standards.

Maintain clear communication cadence with upfitters and stakeholders, tracking milestones and escalating risks as needed.

Define, track, and report on key supply chain performance metrics including, material availability, total cost saving, inventory cycle count accuracy.
Establish programme-level supply chain dashboards and reporting cadences to provide visibility to leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.
Analyse KPI trends to identify root causes of supply chain underperformance and drive corrective actions with suppliers and internal teams.
Leverage KPI insights to continuously improve supply chain processes, reduce waste, and increase overall programme efficiency.

Our customers include Fortune 500 enterprises and global industry leaders, including Anduril, Canva, Fortinet, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, OpenAI, Snap Inc., and Snowflake.
Chainguard is venture-backed by leading investors, including Amplify, IVP, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Mantis VC, Redpoint Ventures, Sequoia Capital, and Spark Capital.

Chainguard's security organization sits at the intersection of proactive, long-term initiatives and reactive, business-critical work. As we've grown, managing that balance, anticipating the downstream impact of changing priorities, and giving leadership a clear view of our security risk and exposure have become increasingly important, and increasingly complex.
We're looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to bring structure and visibility to this space.
You'll operate horizontally across the security organization, partnering with Product Security, Cyber Resiliency, and Governance & Trust. While you'll be closely embedded with those teams in your day-to-day work, you'll also help coordinate priorities, dependencies, and execution across the broader security organization.
Your impact will extend well beyond security. Because security intersects with nearly every function at Chainguard — including engineering, product, legal, finance, sales, and marketing — you'll build the systems, processes, and relationships that enable effective collaboration across the company.
This is a senior, strategic role with substantial room to grow. You won't inherit a fully defined playbook; you'll help create it. You'll establish the processes, dashboards, and prioritization mechanisms that give the security organization greater clarity and leverage, and over time, expand that impact into broader company-wide programs and operating processes.

Own workflow, project tracking, and dependency management across the three security teams, making it clear what’s on track, what’s at risk, and what downstream impact changes may have.
Build and maintain dashboards and reporting that give company leadership a clear, durable view of security risk, exposure, and program health.
Partner closely with your primary security team on day-to-day execution while supporting the other two teams as priorities and capacity allow.
Make and communicate prioritization decisions when demand exceeds the security organization’s capacity — including finding alternatives and helping stakeholders understand trade-offs, rather than simply saying no.
Design and implement lightweight processes that help security teams operate more effectively without creating unnecessary overhead for engineers.
Work directly with product, engineering, and other partner teams to establish clear, effective ways of working with security.
As the role grows, extend your impact beyond security by helping shape broader company processes, including how Chainguard approaches planning, prioritization, and cross-functional execution.

5+ years of experience in program management, technical program management, or operations roles
Meaningful experience in a broad, cross-functional operations or program management role, supporting many stakeholders across an organization rather than working within a single, self-contained team.
Security experience is a plus, but not required. More important is the ability to operate effectively in a horizontal role with a large and diverse stakeholder group.
A track record of building processes and exercising sound judgment in ambiguous environments, rather than defaulting to standard frameworks or playbooks.
Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to act as a strategic and consultative partner across functions.
Experience managing competing priorities and communicating trade-offs, including difficult prioritization decisions, clearly and thoughtfully.
Comfort working in a fast-moving, scaling environment where processes are still being built and refined.

Security work at Chainguard doesn’t follow a predictable schedule. Proactive initiatives and reactive, business-critical needs are constantly competing for the same time and attention. This role exists to bring structure to that tension — helping the security organization make deliberate choices about where to focus and how to respond when priorities inevitably shift.
At the same time, company leadership needs a clearer, more consistent view of our security posture, risk, and exposure than we currently have a dedicated mechanism to provide. You’ll build that reporting infrastructure and make it durable as the organization grows.
And because security intersects with nearly every part of the business, you’ll have an unusually broad view of how Chainguard operates. Over time, you’ll have the opportunity to take what you learn in security and apply it to larger, org-wide programs and processes — helping shape not just how security works, but how Chainguard works as a company.
